ruling.recommended_action: Refund $11.22 to the rider's original payment method as the un-notified surge differential; send the driver the RD-7 notification-duty reminder and log the notification failure on his route-compliance record (no driver violation recorded on the route point, since the off-route segment is exempt as the rider's own requested stop and no traffic reason was available either way). No account flag.
ruling.reasoning:
The complaint is a fare dispute with two components: a surge increase and a route deviation. The fare record settles the surge side: the quote was $23.58 at 1× with a surgeable subtotal of $22.11 [F8], the trip was charged $40.75 at 1.4× from trip start with a surgeable subtotal of $28.06 [F9], the multiplier rose from 1× to 1.4× [F10], and the surge log records that the rider was not notified [F11]. Under SURGE-1 the quote is binding unless the rider is notified in-app before or at pickup of the new multiplier, the revised estimated fare and free cancellation; none was given, so the notice element is not met and SURGE-2 sends the full surge differential back to the rider [F11][SURGE-2]. The differential, as the trace computes and both briefs concede, is (1.4 − 1) × $28.06 = $11.22 [F10][SURGE-3]; the $1.47 booking fee is not surged [F9][FARE-0].

On the route side, the trip ran 13.4 km against a 9.9 km optimal route (+3.5 km) [F1], and the single off-route segment 10:00–10:10 drove 4.65 km where the optimal route covers 1.64 km, adding 3.01 km, over CIRCUIT ROAD → CIRCUIT LINK → PAYA LEBAR ROAD → UBI AVENUE 2 → UBI ROAD 3 → UBI AVENUE 1 [F4]. At 09:56, before the segment began, the rider asked "Can stop at Paya Lebar Square for 5 min?" [F12] and the driver accepted with "Ok" [F13]. The chat record is complete and timestamped [F14]. This is a rider-named place accepted by the driver before the segment, so under RD-3(a) the stop is not a deviation, and reading RD-3 with RD-5 the segment driven to reach that stop — the whole 10:00–10:10 segment, which ends at the stationary stop at 10:03–10:07, 2663 m from pickup [F2] — is exempt in full; the stop time remains chargeable as time fare [F2][F3]. The segments are not to be split into "the stop" and "the way there", so there is no residual non-exempt km to refund.

The driver's post-trip statement that the rider "added a stop" [F15] is consistent with this and does not decide anything beyond it (profile facts, and statements where system records speak, never decide the case). Because the only deviation is exempt under RD-3, no excess-distance refund arises under RD-2, and the RD-4 screen changes nothing here: a traffic reason never exempts a segment, and its only other effect — recording a driver violation for an uninformed reroute [RD-2/RD-4] — is not triggered because the reroute was the rider's own requested stop and she was not uninformed. The refund therefore stands at the surge differential alone.

Safety screen: I read the complaint, both chat messages [F12][F13] and the driver's written statement [F15] in context. The complaint is about money; the messages are a pickup/stop arrangement and a one-word acceptance; the statement is a refund argument. Nothing describes threats, intimidation, harassment, sexual remarks, dangerous driving or anyone feeling unsafe — no safety flag [SAFE-1]. Evidence is sufficient: GPS distance and segment data [F1][F2][F4], fare figures [F5][F7][F8][F9], a complete timestamped chat [F14] and the surge log [F11] settle every element the ruling needs. Amount $11.22 is under $10? No — it is under $50, and this fare case is resolved by the system at confidence ≥ 80% (TH-1, TH-2), consistent with DISP-001/DISP-2026-0142.

The driver's brief concedes this element.

Surge rose and the rider was not notified while she rode [F10][F11], which under SURGE-2 requires full refund of the surge differential; computed under SURGE-3 as (1.4 − 1) × $28.06 = $11.22, booking fee $1.47 excluded [F9][FARE-0].

rejected_claims.reason: The proposed split of the deviation into 'exempt stop km' and 'non-exempt 2.01 km' fails: RD-3 read with RD-5 exempts in full the segment driven to a rider-named stop the car made [F12][F13][F4], so the 1 km RD-1 tolerance and its arithmetic do not apply to carve out refundable km here [RD-3][RD-1].
Correct as far as it goes (no route violation upheld in 90 days [F17], RD-6), but it decides nothing: no account flag is sought or imposed on this record [RD-6][F17].

The $4.84 billed excess distance [F5] is not refundable: the deviation it reflects lies in the segment that was the rider's own requested stop [F4][F12][F13], exempt under RD-3, so no excess-distance refund arises under RD-2.

The premise that 'a stop is not consent to the route' is not the test: the rider named the place and the car stopped there, which under RD-3(a) makes the segment driven to reach it non-deviant in full; the chat is complete and timestamped [F14][F12][F13][F4].

No driver violation is recorded and no excess-distance fare is refunded: RD-2's violation entry attaches to an uninformed reroute without a traffic reason, and here the off-route segment is the rider's own requested stop [F4][F12][F13], while RD-4's incident screen never itself exempts or adds km [RD-2][RD-4].

The $16.06 total is rejected: only the $11.22 un-notified surge differential [F10] is refundable; the $4.84 excess-distance fare falls away because the deviation segment is exempt under RD-3 [F5][F4][F12][F13].
Same as C11: the alternative computation of $16.06 double-counts route km that RD-3 exempts; the remaining $1.11 of the $17.17 gap (base/platform components) is likewise not refundable [F7][F8][F9].
